tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an 18% error rate. Rolled back all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. (v2.3.1-rc was healthy only in staging, so it was not used.) After the rollback: all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident.

- **Version choice:** The release that broke things was v2.3.1, with an 18% error rate in us-east, us-west and eu-west. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. I didn't use v2.3.1-rc because it was only ever healthy in staging, not in production.
- **Rollback:** All three regions are now on v2.3.0. A follow-up status check shows the service is healthy, with the error rate down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001 for checkout-api, which paged on-call. It explains what failed, the rollback, the results afterwards, and the next step: find out why v2.3.1 failed before deploying it again.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0 (v2.3.1-rc was only healthy in staging).
